sanskrit: śārīramānase duḥkhe yo 'tīte anuśocati duḥkhena labhate duḥkhaṃ dvāv anarthau prapadyate
english: He who grieves over bodily or mental pain that is already past gains only more pain by his pain, and so meets with two misfortunes together.

sanskrit: śītoṣṇe caiva vāyuś ca trayaḥ śārīrajā guṇāḥ teṣāṃ guṇānāṃ sāmyaṃ ca tad āhuḥ svasthalakṣaṇam
english: Cold, heat, and wind—these are the three humours born of the body; the balance of these humours is called the mark of health.

sanskrit: teṣām anyatamotseke vidhānam upadiṣyate uṣṇena bādhyate śītaṃ śītenoṣṇaṃ prabādhyate
english: When any one of them grows excessive, a remedy is prescribed: cold is countered by heat, and heat is driven off by cold.

sanskrit: sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva mānasāḥ syus trayo guṇāḥ harṣeṇa bādhyate śoko harṣaḥ śokena bādhyate
english: Goodness (sattva), passion (rajas), and darkness (tamas)—these are the three qualities of the mind; sorrow is countered by joy, and joy is countered by sorrow.

sanskrit: kaś cit sukhe vartamāno duḥkhasya smartum icchati kaś cid duḥkhe vartamānaḥ sukhasya smartum icchati
english: One man, dwelling in happiness, wishes to recall his sorrow; another, dwelling in sorrow, wishes to recall his happiness.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ na duḥkhī duḥkhasya na sukhī ca sukhasya ca na duḥkhī sukhajātasya na sukhī duḥkhajasya vā
english: But you—you are neither one who sorrows over sorrow nor one who rejoices over joy; you are not pained by what springs from joy, nor gladdened by what springs from pain.

sanskrit: smartum arhasi kauravya diṣṭaṃ tu balavattaram atha vā te svabhāvo 'yaṃ yena pārthiva kṛṣyase
english: You ought to remember, O Kaurava, that fate is the stronger force; or else it is this nature of your own, O king, by which you are dragged about.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā sabhāgatāṃ kṛṣṇām ekavastrāṃ rajasvalām miṣatāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ na tasya smartum arhasi
english: You ought not to recall the day when Kṛṣṇā was dragged into the assembly, clad in a single garment and in her courses, before the very eyes of the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: pravrājanaṃ ca nagarād ajinaiś ca nivāsanam mahāraṇyanivāsaś ca na tasya smartum arhasi
english: You ought not to recall our banishment from the city, our dwelling clothed in deerskins, and our long sojourn in the great forest.

sanskrit: jaṭāsurāt parikleśaṃ citrasenena cāhavam saindhavāc ca parikleśaṃ kathaṃ vismṛtavān asi punar ajñātacaryāyāṃ kīcakena padā vadham
english: The torment we suffered from Jaṭāsura, the battle with Citrasena, the affliction at the hands of the lord of the Sindhus, and again, during the year of concealment, the murderous kick of Kīcaka—how have you forgotten these?

sanskrit: yac ca te droṇabhīṣmābhyāṃ yuddham āsīd ariṃdama manasaikena te yuddham idaṃ ghoram upasthitam
english: The war you waged against Droṇa and Bhīṣma, O subduer of foes, is past; but now this dreadful war with your own mind alone has come upon you.

sanskrit: yatra nāsti śaraiḥ kāryaṃ na mitrair na ca bandhubhiḥ ātmanaikena yoddhavyaṃ tat te yuddham upasthitam
english: A war in which there is no use for arrows, nor for friends, nor for kinsmen—a war to be fought by oneself alone—that is the war now set before you.

sanskrit: tasminn anirjite yuddhe prāṇān yadi ha mokṣyase anyaṃ dehaṃ samāsthāya punas tenaiva yotsyase
english: If you give up your life in this war while it is yet unconquered, then, taking up another body, you will have to fight that very same battle once again.

sanskrit: tasmād adyaiva gantavyaṃ yuddhasya bharatarṣabha etaj jitvā mahārāja kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi
english: Therefore this very day you must press to the end of that war, O bull of the Bhāratas; for having won it, great king, you will have accomplished all that is to be done.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ viniścitya bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim pitṛpaitāmahe vṛtte śādhi rājyaṃ yathocitam
english: Having grasped with sure resolve this knowledge of the coming and going of all creatures, govern the kingdom as is fitting, in the way of your fathers and forefathers.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā duryodhanaḥ pāpo nihataḥ sānugo yudhi draupadyāḥ keśapakṣasya diṣṭyā tvaṃ padavīṃ gataḥ
english: By good fortune the wicked Duryodhana, with all his followers, has been slain in battle; by good fortune you have avenged the seizing of Draupadī's hair.

sanskrit: yajasva vājimedhena vidhivad dakṣiṇāvatā vayaṃ te kiṃkarāḥ pārtha vāsudevaś ca vīryavān
english: Offer the horse-sacrifice according to the rite, with its rich gifts to the priests; we are your servants, O Pārtha, and so too is the mighty Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca asaṃtoṣaḥ pramādaś ca mado rāgo 'praśāntatā balaṃ moho 'bhimānaś ca udvegaś cāpi sarvaśaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Discontent, heedlessness, intoxication, passion, restlessness, force, delusion, conceit, and agitation of every kind—

sanskrit: ebhiḥ pāpmabhir āviṣṭo rājyaṃ tvam abhikāṅkṣasi nirāmiṣo vinirmuktaḥ praśāntaḥ susukhī bhava
english: possessed by these vices, you long for sovereignty. Be rid of the lure of the flesh, set free, made calm—and so be truly happy.

sanskrit: ya imām akhilāṃ bhūmiṃ śiṣyād eko mahīpatiḥ tasyāpy udaram evaikaṃ kim idaṃ tvaṃ praśaṃsasi
english: A single sovereign who should rule this whole earth—even he has but one belly to fill; why then do you prize this kingship so?

sanskrit: nāhnā pūrayituṃ śakyā na māsena nararṣabha apūryāṃ pūrayann icchām āyuṣāpi na śaknuyāt
english: Desire cannot be filled in a day, O bull among men, nor in a month; striving to fill the unfillable, a man could not fill it though he spent his whole life.

sanskrit: yatheddhaḥ prajvalaty agnir asamiddhaḥ praśāmyati alpāhāratayā tv agniṃ śamayaudaryam utthitam jayodaraṃ pṛthivyā te śreyo nirjitayā jitam
english: As a fire blazes up when fed and dies down when it is not fed, so by taking little food quell the fire of appetite that has arisen; to conquer the belly is a better conquest than conquering the earth.

sanskrit: mānuṣān kāmabhogāṃs tvam aiśvaryaṃ ca praśaṃsasi abhogino 'balāś caiva yānti sthānam anuttamam
english: You praise the pleasures of human desire and lordly power; yet it is those without enjoyments, those without might, who attain the highest station.

sanskrit: yogakṣemau ca rāṣṭrasya dharmādharmau tvayi sthitau mucyasva mahato bhārāt tyāgam evābhisaṃśraya
english: The welfare and security of the realm, its right and its wrong, all rest upon you; free yourself of this great burden, and take refuge in renunciation alone.

sanskrit: ekodarakṛte vyāghraḥ karoti vighasaṃ bahu tam anye 'py upajīvanti mandavegaṃcarā mṛgāḥ
english: For the sake of one belly the tiger makes a large kill; yet upon its leavings other slow-moving beasts also live.

sanskrit: viṣayān pratisaṃhṛtya saṃnyāsaṃ kurute yatiḥ na ca tuṣyanti rājānaḥ paśya buddhyantaraṃ yathā
english: The ascetic, withdrawing from the objects of sense, practises renunciation; but kings are never satisfied—see how the two ways of mind differ.

sanskrit: patrāhārair aśmakuṭṭair dantolūkhalikais tathā abbhakṣair vāyubhakṣaiś ca tair ayaṃ narako jitaḥ
english: By those who feed on leaves, who grind their food on stones, who use their teeth for a mortar, who live on water or on air alone—by such men has this hell been conquered.

sanskrit: yaś cemāṃ vasudhāṃ kṛtsnāṃ praśāsed akhilāṃ nṛpaḥ tulyāśmakāñcano yaś ca sa kṛtārtho na pārthivaḥ
english: Of the king who should rule this whole earth entire, and the man to whom a stone and gold are alike—it is the latter, not the monarch, who has attained his end.

sanskrit: saṃkalpeṣu nirārambho nirāśo nirmamo bhava viśokaṃ sthānam ātiṣṭha iha cāmutra cāvyayam
english: In your designs be free of undertakings, free of craving, free of the sense of "mine"; take your stand in that state which is without sorrow, imperishable here and hereafter.

sanskrit: nirāmiṣā na śocanti śocasi tvaṃ kim āmiṣam parityajyāmiṣaṃ sarvaṃ mṛṣāvādāt pramokṣyase
english: Those free of the bait of the flesh do not grieve; for what worldly lure do you grieve? Renouncing all such lure, you will be set free even from falsehood.

sanskrit: panthānau pitṛyānaś ca devayānaś ca viśrutau ījānāḥ pitṛyānena devayānena mokṣiṇaḥ
english: Two paths are famed: the way of the fathers and the way of the gods; those who sacrifice go by the way of the fathers, but those who seek release go by the way of the gods.

sanskrit: tapasā brahmacaryeṇa svādhyāyena ca pāvitāḥ vimucya dehān vai bhānti mṛtyor aviṣayaṃ gatāḥ
english: Purified by austerity, by chastity, and by study of the sacred texts, they cast off their bodies and shine forth, having passed beyond the reach of death.

sanskrit: āmiṣaṃ bandhanaṃ loke karmehoktaṃ tathāmiṣam tābhyāṃ vimuktaḥ pāśābhyāṃ padam āpnoti tatparam
english: The lure of the world is one bond, and worldly action is called another such lure; freed from both these snares, a man attains that supreme station.

sanskrit: api gāthām imāṃ gītāṃ janakena vadanty uta nirdvaṃdvena vimuktena mokṣaṃ samanupaśyatā
english: Indeed, men recite this verse that was sung by Janaka—a king beyond the pairs of opposites, liberated, and looking clearly upon release:

sanskrit: anantaṃ bata me vittaṃ yasya me nāsti kiṃ cana mithilāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ na me dahyati kiṃ cana
english: "Boundless, indeed, is my wealth, I who own nothing at all; though Mithilā be ablaze, nothing of mine is burned."

sanskrit: prajñāprāsādam āruhya naśocyāñ śocato janān jagatīsthān ivādristho mandabuddhīn avekṣate
english: Mounting the tower of wisdom, he looks down upon dull-witted men who grieve over things not to be grieved for, as one standing on a mountain looks down upon those below on the earth.

sanskrit: dṛśyaṃ paśyati yaḥ paśyan sa cakṣuṣmān sa buddhimān ajñātānāṃ ca vijñānāt saṃbodhād buddhir ucyate
english: He who, while seeing, truly sees what is to be seen—he has eyes, he has understanding; and from the discerning of things not yet known, from awakening, is true intelligence said to arise.

sanskrit: yas tu vācaṃ vijānāti bahumānam iyāt sa vai brahmabhāvaprasūtānāṃ vaidyānāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: He who rightly understands the word would surely come to high honour among the learned, whose souls are perfected and who are born of the state of Brahman.

sanskrit: yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvam ekastham anupaśyati tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When a man perceives the manifold being of all creatures as resting in one, and their unfolding as proceeding from that very oneness, then he attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: te janās tāṃ gatiṃ yānti nāvidvāṃso 'lpacetasaḥ nābuddhayo nātapasaḥ sarvaṃ buddhau pratiṣṭhitam
english: Such men reach that goal—not the ignorant, not the feeble of mind, not the witless, not those without austerity; for everything is established upon understanding.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tūṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ tu rājānaṃ punar evārjuno 'bravīt saṃtaptaḥ śokaduḥkhābhyāṃ rājño vākśalyapīḍitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But to the king, who had fallen silent, Arjuna spoke once more—himself scorched by grief and sorrow, pierced by the barbed words of the king.

sanskrit: kathayanti purāvṛttam itihāsam imaṃ janāḥ videharājñaḥ saṃvādaṃ bhāryayā saha bhārata
english: Men tell this ancient tale of long ago, O Bhārata—the dialogue of the king of Videha with his wife.

sanskrit: utsṛjya rājyaṃ bhaikṣārthaṃ kṛtabuddhiṃ janeśvaram videharājaṃ mahiṣī duḥkhitā pratyabhāṣata
english: When the lord of men, the king of Videha, had cast off his kingdom and resolved upon a life of begging, his queen, sorrowing, addressed him thus.

sanskrit: dhanāny apatyaṃ mitrāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca panthānaṃ pāvanaṃ hitvā janako mauṇḍyam āsthitaḥ
english: Forsaking riches, offspring, friends, jewels of every kind, and the hallowing path of duty, Janaka had taken to the shaven head of the mendicant.

sanskrit: taṃ dadarśa priyā bhāryā bhaikṣyavṛttim akiṃcanam dhānāmuṣṭim upāsīnaṃ nirīhaṃ gatamatsaram
english: His beloved wife beheld him living by alms, owning nothing, seated with a mere fistful of grain, without effort and without envy.

sanskrit: tam uvāca samāgamya bhartāram akutobhayam kruddhā manasvinī bhāryā vivikte hetumad vacaḥ
english: Coming up to her lord, who now feared nothing from any quarter, the high-spirited wife, in her anger, spoke to him in private these reasoned words:

sanskrit: katham utsṛjya rājyaṃ svaṃ dhanadhānyasamācitam kāpālīṃ vṛttim āsthāya dhānāmuṣṭir vane 'caraḥ
english: "How is it that, having abandoned your own kingdom, heaped with wealth and grain, you take up the life of a beggar with his bowl and roam the forest with a fistful of grain?

sanskrit: pratijñā te 'nyathā rājan viceṣṭā cānyathā tava yad rājyaṃ mahad utsṛjya svalpe tuṣyasi pārthiva
english: Your vow, O king, is one thing, and your conduct quite another, in that you forsake a great kingdom and content yourself with a trifle, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: naitenātithayo rājan devarṣipitaras tathā śakyam adya tvayā bhartuṃ moghas te 'yaṃ pariśramaḥ
english: With this, O king, you can today maintain neither guests, nor the gods, the sages, and the ancestors; this toil of yours is fruitless.

sanskrit: devatātithibhiś caiva pitṛbhiś caiva pārthiva sarvair etaiḥ parityaktaḥ parivrajasi niṣkriyaḥ
english: Forsaken by all of these—by the gods, by guests, and by the ancestors, O king—you wander forth, doing nothing.

sanskrit: yas tvaṃ traividyavṛddhānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasraśaḥ bhartā bhūtvā ca lokasya so 'dyānyair bhṛtim icchasi
english: You who were once the sustainer of thousands of aged brāhmaṇas learned in the three Vedas, and of all the world—do you now seek your living from others?

sanskrit: śriyaṃ hitvā pradīptāṃ tvaṃ śvavat saṃprati vīkṣyase aputrā jananī te 'dya kausalyā cāpatis tvayā
english: Casting off your blazing royal splendour, you are now looked upon like a dog; this day your mother is made sonless, and Kausalyā is made husbandless by you.

sanskrit: aśītir dharmakāmās tvāṃ kṣatriyāḥ paryupāsate tvadāśām abhikāṅkṣantyaḥ kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetukāḥ
english: Eighty kṣatriyas, longing for righteousness, wait upon you, craving your favour—wretched men, intent upon reward.

sanskrit: tāś ca tvaṃ viphalāḥ kurvan kāṃl lokān nu gamiṣyasi rājan saṃśayite mokṣe paratantreṣu dehiṣu
english: By rendering their hopes fruitless, to what worlds will you go, O king, when release is uncertain and all embodied beings are bound to dependence?

sanskrit: naiva te 'sti paro loko nāparaḥ pāpakarmaṇaḥ dharmyān dārān parityajya yas tvam icchasi jīvitum
english: For you there is no higher world, nor any other—you sinner in deed—who, forsaking a lawful wife, wish to go on living thus.

sanskrit: srajo gandhān alaṃkārān vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca kimartham abhisaṃtyajya parivrajasi niṣkriyaḥ
english: Garlands, perfumes, ornaments, and garments of every kind—for what purpose have you cast all these away to wander forth, doing nothing?

sanskrit: nipānaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ bhūtvā tvaṃ pāvanaṃ mahat āḍhyo vanaspatir bhūtvā so 'dyānyān paryupāsase
english: Having been a great and hallowing watering-place for all creatures, a richly laden forest-tree, do you now wait upon others?

sanskrit: khādanti hastinaṃ nyāse kravyādā bahavo 'py uta bahavaḥ kṛmayaś caiva kiṃ punas tvām anarthakam
english: When an elephant is laid out dead, many flesh-eating beasts devour it, and many worms as well; how much more, then, would they make away with one as useless as you?

sanskrit: ya imāṃ kuṇḍikāṃ bhindyāt triviṣṭabdhaṃ ca te haret vāsaś cāpaharet tasmin kathaṃ te mānasaṃ bhavet
english: If someone should break this water-pot of yours, carry off your three-staved support, and take away your garment—how then would your mind be set toward him?

sanskrit: yas tv ayaṃ sarvam utsṛjya dhānāmuṣṭiparigrahaḥ yadānena samaṃ sarvaṃ kim idaṃ mama dīyate dhānāmuṣṭir ihārthaś cet pratijñā te vinaśyati
english: He who has cast off everything yet still clings to a fistful of grain—if a fistful of grain is one with the whole of his wealth, then why is even this given to me? And if a fistful of grain is here your object, then your vow is undone.

sanskrit: kā vāhaṃ tava ko me tvaṃ ko 'dya te mayy anugrahaḥ praśādhi pṛthivīṃ rājan yatra te 'nugraho bhavet prāsādaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca
english: What, then, am I to you, and what are you to me? What favour have you now toward me? Rule the earth, O king, in which your grace might find its place—palace, couch, chariot, garments, and ornaments.

sanskrit: śriyā nirāśair adhanais tyaktamitrair akiṃcanaiḥ saukhikaiḥ saṃbhṛtān arthān yaḥ saṃtyajasi kiṃ nu tat
english: That you should cast away wealth gathered for the sake of comfort—by men hopeless of fortune, destitute, forsaken by friends, owning nothing—what, then, is the meaning of this?

sanskrit: yo 'tyantaṃ pratigṛhṇīyād yaś ca dadyāt sadaiva hi tayos tvam antaraṃ viddhi śreyāṃs tābhyāṃ ka ucyate
english: He who would forever be taking, and he who would forever be giving—know the difference between these two, and tell which of them is called the better.

sanskrit: sadaiva yācamāneṣu satsu dambhavivarjiṣu eteṣu dakṣiṇā dattā dāvāgnāv iva durhutam
english: A gift bestowed upon such men—worthy and free of pretence, yet forever begging—is like an offering ill-poured into a forest fire.

sanskrit: jātavedā yathā rājann ādagdhvaivopaśāmyati sadaiva yācamāno vai tathā śāmyati na dvijaḥ
english: As the fire, O king, dies down only after it has burnt all to ashes, so the brāhmaṇa who is forever begging never finds his fill.

sanskrit: satāṃ ca vedā annaṃ ca loke 'smin prakṛtir dhruvā na ced dātā bhaved dātā kutaḥ syur mokṣakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: The Vedas and food of the virtuous are the fixed order of things in this world; if there were no giver to give, whence would there arise those who seek release?

sanskrit: annād gṛhasthā loke 'smin bhikṣavas tata eva ca annāt prāṇaḥ prabhavati annadaḥ prāṇado bhavet
english: From food come householders in this world, and from them, in turn, the mendicants; from food springs life itself, so the giver of food is the giver of life.

sanskrit: gṛhasthebhyo 'bhinirvṛttā gṛhasthān eva saṃśritāḥ prabhavaṃ ca pratiṣṭhāṃ ca dāntā nindanta āsate
english: Risen from householders, and depending upon householders still, these self-restrained men sit reviling the very source and ground of their being.

sanskrit: tyāgān na bhikṣukaṃ vidyān na mauṇḍyān na ca yācanāt ṛjus tu yo 'rthaṃ tyajati taṃ sukhaṃ viddhi bhikṣukam
english: One should not know the true mendicant by renunciation alone, nor by the shaven head, nor by begging; but he who, with an honest heart, gives up wealth—know him for the mendicant who is truly at ease.

sanskrit: asaktaḥ saktavad gacchan niḥsaṅgo muktabandhanaḥ samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca sa vai mukto mahīpate
english: Unattached, yet moving among men as though attached; free of clinging, his bonds undone; the same toward foe and friend—he, O lord of the earth, is truly the liberated one.

sanskrit: parivrajanti dānārthaṃ muṇḍāḥ kāṣāyavāsasaḥ sitā bahuvidhaiḥ pāśaiḥ saṃcinvanto vṛthāmiṣam
english: Shaven-headed and clad in ochre robes, they wander forth for the sake of alms, bound by snares of many kinds, gathering up the empty bait of the world.

sanskrit: trayīṃ ca nāma vārtāṃ ca tyaktvā putrāṃs tyajanti ye triviṣṭabdhaṃ ca vāsaś ca pratigṛhṇanty abuddhayaḥ
english: Those witless men who, forsaking the threefold Veda and their livelihood, abandon even their sons, yet still accept the three-staved support and a garment—

sanskrit: aniṣkaṣāye kāṣāyam īhārtham iti viddhi tat dharmadhvajānāṃ muṇḍānāṃ vṛttyartham iti me matiḥ
english: know that the ochre robe upon one not purged of passion is but a means to getting; the shaven heads of these flaunters of piety, I hold, serve only to win them a living.

sanskrit: kāṣāyair ajinaiś cīrair nagnān muṇḍāñ jaṭādharān bibhrat sādhūn mahārāja jaya lokāñ jitendriyaḥ
english: Sustaining holy men—the naked, the shaven, and the matted-haired—with ochre robes, deerskins, and bark garments, O great king, master your senses and win the worlds.

sanskrit: agnyādheyāni gurvarthān kratūn sapaśudakṣiṇān dadāty aharahaḥ pūrvaṃ ko nu dharmataras tataḥ
english: He who day after day, as of old, establishes the sacred fires, serves the needs of his elders, and offers sacrifices with their gifts of cattle—who, then, is more righteous than he?

sanskrit: tattvajño janako rājā loke 'sminn iti gīyate so 'py āsīn mohasaṃpanno mā mohavaśam anvagāḥ
english: King Janaka is sung of in this world as one who knows the truth of things; yet even he was once overcome by delusion—do not you fall under the sway of delusion.

sanskrit: evaṃ dharmam anukrāntaṃ sadā dānaparair naraiḥ ānṛśaṃsyaguṇopetaiḥ kāmakrodhavivarjitāḥ
english: Thus is the duty followed by men ever devoted to giving, endowed with the virtue of compassion, and free of desire and wrath—

sanskrit: pālayantaḥ prajāś caiva dānam uttamam āsthitāḥ iṣṭāṃl lokān avāpsyāmo brahmaṇyāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: "protecting our subjects and holding fast to the highest giving, devoted to the brāhmaṇas and speakers of truth, we shall attain the worlds we long for."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vedāhaṃ tāta śāstrāṇi aparāṇi parāṇi ca ubhayaṃ vedavacanaṃ kuru karma tyajeti ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I know the scriptures, my dear brother, both the lower and the higher; I know too the twofold word of the Veda—"perform action" and "renounce action."

sanskrit: ākulāni ca śāstrāṇi hetubhiś citritāni ca niścayaś caiva yanmātro vedāhaṃ taṃ yathāvidhi
english: The scriptures are tangled and embroidered over with conflicting reasons; and the sure conclusion, of whatever measure it be, I know in due form.
